newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ZAGALLO SAYS HE WILL NOT RELEASE ROBERTO CARLOS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALLO SAYS HE WILL NOT RELEASE ROBERTO CARLOS.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said on Friday he would not allow full-back Roberto Carlos to play in a Spanish championship match which coincides with the national team's European tour.

Zagallo said Roberto Carlos had sought permission to play for his club Real Madrid in between Brazil's friendly with Norway in Oslo on May 30 and their match against France in the French city of Lyon on June 3.
"There's no way of releasing him for this game. He's a regular in our team and there won't be time," Zagallo said. "I just can't do it."
Brazil lost a similar tug-of-war match with Deportivo Coruna, another Spanish club, two years ago when they refused to release striker Bebeto for a tournament in England.

Last year, when the same club claimed that midfielder Mauro Silva was unfit to play in a friendly in Brazil, Zagallo ordered the player to make a transatlantic journey to be examined by the Brazil team doctor.
Mauro Silva was not passed fit and travelled from Coruna to the Brazilian city of Curitiba and straight back again.
Brazil face a hectic schedule, which begins with the Oslo game.
They then play in a four-team tournament in France between June 3 and 10 and just three days later make their debut in the Copa America in the Bolivian city of Santa Cruz.
They could play six games in the Copa America if they reach the final.
